name: Voice coach / speech therapy

lead: Voice coaching and speech therapy are professional services for changing how a voice sounds or functions, from speech-language pathologists or voice teachers. People use them to adjust pitch, quality and delivery so their voice matches the image they want.

Therapists and teachers guide exercises on breath, pitch, resonance and vocal fold closure. The field is established: voice therapy is mainly used for voice disorders and is also used in transgender voice therapy, and published evidence is described as limited and varying by method. No studies test coaching for appearance goals in people without voice disorders.

paras: People book sessions with a speech-language pathologist or voice teacher, record their voice, and practise assigned exercises between visits. Programmes commonly run over several weeks to months and combine breathing, pitch and resonance work.
No notable harms are documented. Cost and the time needed for regular practice are the main practical considerations.

angle.text: A voice coach or speech-language pathologist can train pitch, resonance and delivery so your voice sounds the way you want. It is the same route used in transgender voice therapy. The clinical field is established, with research centred on voice disorders.

lead: Voice coaching and speech therapy refer to professional services used to change how a voice sounds or functions. Voice therapy is provided mainly by speech-language pathologists, who target vocal parameters such as vocal fold closure, pitch, volume and quality, chiefly to manage voice disorders, but also to change overall voice quality, as in transgender voice therapy.[1] Vocal pedagogy, taught by voice teachers, is the related field focused on singing.[1][2]

In looksmaxxing discussion, professional voice help is mentioned as a route to a different-sounding voice. Published evidence on voice therapy is described as limited and varies by method.[1] No studies were found testing voice coaching for appearance in people without voice disorders.
infobox: Resonant voice therapy, Accent Method, vocal hygiene

paras: Voice therapy orientations include symptomatic, physiologic, hygienic, psychogenic and eclectic approaches, and treatment is individualised to the disorder and the person.[1] Techniques include the Accent Method (diaphragmatic breathing with rhythmic vowel play), chant-talk, resonant voice therapy, REST exercises and vocal hygiene advice.[1]
Voice teachers build technique across breath, phonation, resonance, articulation and range, and may also teach microphone use and performance skills.[2]

No studies found on coaching for appearance in healthy people. Within speech pathology, systematic reviews of resonant voice therapy (Yiu and colleagues, 2016) and of voice therapy for dysphonia (Drake and colleagues, 2016) exist, and one 2013 paper questioned its effectiveness for children's vocal fold nodules.[1]
